label: GO step after a rewarded trial, strongly committed to a2, late in the episode (trial >= ~70)
explanation: Fires only at GO (never D1/D2), only when the previous trial was rewarded (99% of mass), and almost only when the agent is about to choose a2 (policy logit strongly favoring a2; action==2 holds 100% of mass). It is also gated by time in the episode: essentially silent before trial ~55, ramping up through trials 60-99, so it is a late-episode, rewarded-and-choosing-a2 feature (consistent with low value-head output). The equivalent predicate using the upcoming action (action == 2) instead of the policy logit scores dev F1 0.85; the logit version (choice < -6, the agent own computed policy, not a future random outcome) scores 0.89 and is recorded. Does not fire after unrewarded trials, on a1 choices, or early in episodes. Misses are mostly weak activations on trials 60-69 or after unrewarded trials; magnitude was not characterised beyond the time ramp.

issues: Most claims hold. Activity is GO-only, with 0 active steps at D1 and D2. 98.9% of activation mass has prev_reward==1. action==2 holds 100% of mass (3 active steps on a1). Firing is 0 before trial 50, 0.4% on trials 50-59, then rises from 3.1% to 12.3% over trials 60-99. The dev scores reproduce: P 0.942, R 0.836, F1 0.886, mass recall 0.958.

There is one systematic false-positive class: a rare-rewarded previous trial (a2 reached S1 and was rewarded). Within the predicate, test precision is 0.44 when prev_common==0 (3135 predicted steps) against 0.987 when prev_common==1 (26621 steps). That class alone produces about 1750 of the 2330 test false positives. So the feature is not driven by 'a rewarded trial' in general. It is driven by a reward collected in S2 after a common a2 transition, and it is mostly suppressed after a rare-rewarded a2 trial. The label overclaims by saying just 'after a rewarded trial'.

Adding (prev_common != 0) raises test precision to 0.983 but lowers recall to 0.800, so F1 stays about the same (0.882). Rare-rewarded steps fire weakly about half the time, so the gap shows up in precision, not F1.

The trial >= 70 cutoff is arbitrary. choice < -7 with ep_trial >= 66 does slightly better (dev 0.898, test 0.893). The 'late in episode' term is interchangeable with low value: replacing ep_trial with value < 7.2 gives dev F1 0.879. So the time dependence may really be a value dependence; the explanation hints at this but does not settle it.
Precision is lower when good == S1 (0.81, the agent still on a2 after a reversal) than when good == S2 (0.95). This is a minor effect.
Misses are as described: weak activations (about 0.05-0.2 of max) after unrewarded trials or on trials 60-69, which hold only 4.4% of mass on test.
skeptic.revised_label: GO step late in the episode (trial >= ~66, low value) when the agent is strongly committed to a2 and the previous trial was a2 rewarded in S2 (common); mostly suppressed when the previous reward came after a rare transition to S1
